title: Attribution Graphs of a Refusal Decision in an Open Model

original_idea.body:
# Attribution Graphs of a Refusal Decision in an Open Model

**Problem:** Circuit tracing showcased on factual recall and poetry; the computation producing a safety refusal and where a jailbreak diverts it is unmapped with open attribution-graph tooling.

**Direction:** Using open Circuit Tracer on a supported model, build attribution graphs for a refused harmful request vs the same under a successful jailbreak; identify suppressed/rerouted features.

**Why it matters:** Pinpoints the mechanistic pressure point of refusal for hardening safety. Reproducible outside labs.

**Relevant context:** transformer-circuits.pub 2025; Circuit Tracer; jailbreak datasets.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: locating the refusal pressure point directly informs hardening against jailbreaks, a critical safety pathway.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Attribution-graph interpretation is intermediate; requires solid mech-interp fundamentals despite released tooling.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused contrast (refused vs jailbroken) on one model with clear identification goal.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Released tooling, open model, refusal-circuit mapping labs underpublish; independent-friendly.

low_compute.reasoning: Attribution graphs on a small open model; single mid GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Refusal directions are studied; full attribution-graph mapping in open models may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Refusal mechanisms studied broadly; attribution-graph open-model mapping may be open.
